{{legend0|#808080|TBD Result}} }} The '''2026 United States House of Representatives elections''' were held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, as part of the [[2026 United States elections|2026 midterm elections]] during President [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second nonconsecutive term]]. Voters elected representatives from all 435 [[List of United States congressional districts|congressional districts]] across each of the fifty [[U.S. state]]s, and five of the six [[Non-voting members of the United States House of Representatives|non-voting delegates]] from the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]] and the inhabited [[Insular area|U.S. territories]]. Special elections are also being held on dates throughout 2026. Numerous other federal, state, and local elections, including [[2026 United States Senate elections|elections to the Senate]], were also held on November 3, 2026. The winners of this election will serve in the [[120th United States Congress]], with seats apportioned among the states based on the [[2020 United States census]] and revised district maps as a result of the [[2025–2026 United States redistricting]]. Primary elections for all 435 House seats, and five of the six non-voting delegate seats were held starting on March 3, and concluded on September 15, 2026. With results pending on some districts, the Democratic Party is expected to win a majority for the first time since 2022, with analysts and major networks projecting a "[[Wave elections in the United States|blue tsunami]]" that was "generational in scope" and described the results as "the end of the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump era]]", and [[Trumpism|Donald Trump's ideology]] as "an utterly spent political force" in American politics.{{Cite web |date=2026-11-03|title=2026 Midterm Elections: Live Updates|url=https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/11/2026-midterm-elections-live-updates/|access-date=2026-11-04|website=National Review|language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2026-11-04 |title=Democrats win control of the House of Representatives with a vow to combat Trump |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-house-control-midterm-election-wins-trump-check-rcna603397 |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=NBC News |language=en}} == Results == === Federal === {| class=wikitable ! style="background:#e9e9e9; text-align:center" rowspan="2" colspan="2" | Parties ! style="background:#e9e9e9; text-align:center" colspan="3" | Popular vote ! style="background:#e9e9e9; text-align:center" colspan="4" | Seats |- style="background:#e9e9e9" ! In 2026, most states will use the same districts created in the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting cycle following the 2020 census]], which were first used in the 2022 elections. Maps have changed or would change in several states, often due to legal challenges made based on partisan or racial [[Gerrymandering in the United States|gerrymandering]].{{Table alignment}} As of {{monthyear}}, several states have seen challenges to their [[List of United States congressional districts|congressional district]] maps that were put in place during the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting cycle]] brought upon by the results of the 2020 census. In [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Arkansas|Arkansas]], a federal court dismissed a case against their congressional map that argued the map did not comply with the [[Voting Rights Act]].{{cite web |last=Grajeda |first=Antoinette |date=2025-06-06 |title=Federal panel rules in favor of state in Arkansas congressional redistricting lawsuit |url=https://arkansasadvocate.com/2025/06/06/federal-panel-rules-in-favor-of-state-in-arkansas-congressional-redistricting-lawsuit/ |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Arkansas Advocate |language=en-US}} The [[Supreme Court of Florida|Florida Supreme Court]] dismissed a challenge regarding the Florida's congressional map, finding a new plurality-Black congressional district would be against federal law.{{cite web |title=In boon for House GOP, Florida Supreme Court sides with DeSantis, upholds congressional map |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/07/17/florida-supreme-court-sides-with-desantis-upholds-congressional-map-00459893 |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Politico |date=July 17, 2025}} In [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia|Georgia]], litigation is still ongoing regarding appeals to the newly drawn congressional map that was used in the 2024 elections. However, it was not resolved before the filing deadline for the 2026 Congressional elections.{{cite web |last=Cook |first=Brianna |date=2025-01-22 |title=Georgia's redistricting maps return to court, challenging voting rights protections |url=https://wgxa.tv/news/state-news/georgias-redistricting-maps-return-to-court-challenging-voting-rights-protections-gerrymandering-legislative-congressional-brad-raffensperger |access-date=2025-07-23 |publisher=WGXA |language=en}} In [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Louisiana|Louisiana]], litigation remained unresolved.{{cite web |last=Howe |first=Amy |date=2025-06-27 |title=Supreme Court punts decision on Louisiana's congressional map to next term
